top_problem: The deck runs on two spacing systems: the featured card uses a 96 pt item pitch with 36 pt gaps and 49.5 pt above mid-card subheads, while the three right cards pack items at 0 pt gaps with subheads 1.5 pt under the previous description. The left column looks like it has holes and the right column looks crammed, which fails the subheader-spacing check. The boldest missing idea is real lotería cards: numbered portrait cards in the tabla's proportion with a full-bleed figure, not rectangular boxes with a small icon in the corner.
fixes: Use one vertical rhythm on every card: a fixed 12 pt space above each item and 24 pt above every subhead after the first. That makes subhead spacing 13.5/24/24 everywhere (it is currently 49.5 vs 1.5), and the check passes.

Use one type size for item names, prices and descriptions on all four cards, and signal the featured card only through its face and figure. The geometry shows 15.75 vs 13.5 pt name boxes and 13.5 vs 11.5 pt prices, which reads as two menus.

To fill the left card, set the 36 pt free space as one extra 12 pt line under each cocktail rather than as uneven voids, or return the height to the face. The Manhattan-to-House-Originals gap (49.5 pt) should match the Margarita-to-Manhattan gap (39.75 pt).
Give the IOWA CITY, IOWA line at least 12 pt (one baseline) clear of the card tops. It currently sits 2.74 pt above the frames and looks jammed.

Push the lotería concept further: number each card, draw the right-card figures at least 50% of the face width rather than 60 pt corner icons, and use the tabla's card proportion so the idea is unmistakable rather than four framed boxes.

top_problem: The header hierarchy is correct but the spacing around it has collapsed. On the right cards the subheaders (BRANDY, CIDER, SPARKLING) sit on the previous description with 0 pt above, so they read as body text, not section breaks. The featured card floats its items in 36 pt voids with a big hole above HOUSE ORIGINALS. The masthead's IOWA CITY line sits 2.7 pt from the deck. Missing bold idea: the lotería card is only used as a header panel. The cards never become real playing cards (numbered corner indices, a tabla grid and the caller's rhythm driving how you read).
fixes: Use one subheader rhythm on every card: 12 pt (one baseline) above every subheader after the first and 12 pt below, so BRANDY, CIDER and SPARKLING stop sitting on the description above.

Bring the featured card's 36 pt item gap down to 12 pt, the same as the right cards. Give the space you get back to the face or a fifth cocktail, so the left card has no dead holes and the Cantarito name bar can sit on the same row as the El Barril bar (y 384).
Put 12 to 24 pt between the IOWA CITY, IOWA line and the deck top. Right now it touches the cards and the masthead does not read as its own tier.
Use one price size (11.5 pt) on every card, or else make every featured-card element one step larger. Only the prices and names are larger now, so the featured card looks like a different menu.

Make the lotería idea carry the structure: give each card a numbered corner index and consistent card proportions, so the headers work as card faces and not as coloured bars on a generic two-column list.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling
top_problem: Measurements pass: price right edges are exact at 288 pt and 564 pt (±0.0), item names share one left edge at 48 pt and 324 pt, and ink margins are 36 pt on all four sides. Contrast passes: ink 13.4 to 15.6:1, terracotta 5.1 to 5.9:1, muted 6.7 to 7.8:1, cream on terracotta 5.9:1 and cream on agave 6.9:1. The palette is not doing its job, though. Terracotta fills three of the four name bars and is also the colour of every price and every cocktail serve cue. That leaves the prices with no colour of their own. Rosa and marigold appear only in the flags and figures, so the four-colour lotería palette reads as one terracotta template. The boldest missing idea: give each card its own lotería identity. La Rosa's bar and face should be rosa, La Botella's should be ink or dark marigold, and El Barril stays agave. Then each price would pick up its card colour, so colour tells the reader where they are and gives the numbers a signature. Other visible problems: the featured cocktail card has 96 pt item pitch against 24 pt on the right cards, which leaves dead air under Manhattan and Daiquiri. The Iowa City line sits 2.74 pt above the card tops.
fixes: Give each card its own colour: La Rosa bar and face in rosa #C2185B (about 5.2:1 with cream text, so it passes), La Botella in ink #231B16 or a dark marigold that passes 4.5:1, and El Barril stays agave. Terracotta stays only on El Cantarito.
Set each card's prices in that card's colour and set the cocktail serve cues in muted #5A4A3F italic instead of terracotta, so the prices are the only accent-coloured numbers on the page.

Use one price size everywhere (13.5 pt featured against 11.5 pt elsewhere reads as two systems). Replace the default dotted leaders, which end at ragged x positions because the price widths differ (6.5 pt to 15.9 pt), with fixed-width right-aligned price slots or a short marigold-dark rule that ends 6 pt before a fixed price box.

Tighten the cocktail card to a constant visible gap (Manhattan's 2-line block currently sits on the same 96 pt pitch as Margarita's 3-line block) and put the recovered space into the featured face or a fifth cocktail. The goal is a filled card, not white holes.

Open the gap between 'IOWA CITY, IOWA' and the card tops to one full 12 pt baseline (it is 2.74 pt now), and bring marigold into the type system as a dark tone (for example the subheader rules or the ampersand), so the fourth palette colour is more than flag trim.

top_problem: The lotería idea shows up as a label rather than a system. The cards are not proportioned, numbered or illustrated like real lotería cards, and the featured cocktail card is mostly empty space while the right column is crammed. The boldest missing idea is to build the whole sheet as a true lotería tabla: real lotería-proportion cards with numbered corners, full-bleed figures and a caller's-card masthead in place of the stock papel picado string.
fixes: Fix the spacing above subheaders so every header has the same space above it on every card (for example 12 pt above BRANDY, CIDER and SPARKLING, matching CLASSICS), and remove the roughly 140 pt void above HOUSE ORIGINALS.

Rebalance density: close the dead space on the featured card by either growing the cantarito face to real card-art scale or moving a section into the left column, so both columns share one item rhythm (the same gap, not 36 pt against 0 pt).

Make the cards read as real lotería cards: tall card proportions, a numbered corner (for example 13, 32, 47), a heavy black keyline and full-width figures on the right cards instead of 60 x 33 pt icons squeezed beside the verse.

Replace the generic papel picado string with a venue-owned masthead, such as a caller's card or a tabla grid with the bar name set in lotería-style lettering, so the menu cannot be mistaken for any other cantina.
Add at least 12 pt between IOWA CITY, IOWA and the card tops (currently 2.74 pt) so the masthead breathes and sits on the baseline grid.

top_problem: Print and phone are two different card systems: the phone gives every card a big centred lotería face with even item spacing, while print crams three right cards into 0-gap lists with thumbnail figures and leaves the featured card full of dead space, so the bold idea missing is a true lotería tabla: every card a real numbered lotería card (number corner, framed figure, name cartouche) built on ONE modular card unit that tiles 2x2 in print and stacks 1:1 on the phone.
fixes: Use one item rhythm across the deck (for example a 6 pt or 12 pt gap under every description on every card, print and phone) and redistribute the featured card's 36 pt voids, so the left card stops looking empty and the right cards stop looking crushed.

Make the print right-card faces the same system as the phone (centred figure, verse above, cartouche below, at a reduced but proportional height) so the phone reads as the print deck stacked, not a different design.
Add a top safe margin to the phone papel picado string and cut the phone title about 10% so it clears the 390 px side margins by at least 16 px.
Use one price size in print (drop the 13.5 pt featured price to 11.5 pt, or raise all four) to match the phone, where every price is one size.

Push the lotería concept past icons in frames: add card numbers or corner indices, a printed card-edge border with rounded corners, and richer cut-paper figures with more detail, so the cards read as lotería cards rather than flat clip-art tiles.

lens: every item and price vs the draft (build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: All 14 draft items and prices are on the menu and match. The content is still unbalanced. The featured cocktail card gets rich copy with serve cues, and large dead gaps sit between its four items. The other 10 items are crammed into the right column with one- or two-word lines: 'Dry red.', 'Dry white.', 'Dry and sparkling.' twice, and wording like 'Añejo-class tequila' that reads like a category label. So beer has no ABV, wine has no region, spirits have no age or brand, and every category but cocktails reads as an afterthought. Other points: Brut Rosé still prints without a glass or bottle label. The order is Cocktails, Spirits, Beer & Cider, Wine, when the usual flow is cocktails, beer, wine, spirits. The garnish and glass cues (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel, coupe) are cited only as 'recipe' with no row ids and are not in the draft snapshot. Only Cocktail Cherry is in the draft.
fixes: Get the venue to answer the missing_ingredients questions (beer ABV and brewery, wine region and producer, añejo age and brand, cognac house, pour sizes). Until then, write fuller guest-language lines for these items from the draft words. Replace taxonomy wording like 'Añejo-class tequila' and 'Grape brandy, VSOP grade', and stop using 'Dry and sparkling.' for both the cider and the Brut Rosé.

Rebalance the columns so every drinks category gets equal care. Cut the empty space between the cocktail items, or move a section into the left column under the cocktails, so the right-column cards are not tight while El Cantarito has about 80 px of dead space between each item.

Label the Brut Rosé price 'glass' or 'bottle' once the venue answers. Until then, keep it visibly flagged in proposal.md as blocking publication, because an unlabelled price next to a 'By the Glass' list will be read as a glass price.

Add the gateway recipe_version row ids to the proposal.md source table for 'lime wheel', 'lime coin', 'orange peel' and 'coupe', or drop those cues. They are not in the draft snapshot, and the table currently says 'Gateway row ids: none'.

Reorder the right column to Beer & Cider, Wine, Spirits, or state in proposal.md why agave spirits come first for this cantina. Also keep the draft's Manhattan-then-Margarita order in Classics unless the venue approves the swap.

top_problem: The descriptions are only complete on the cocktail card. The other 10 of 14 items are two- or three-word fragments with no style + ABV (beer), region (wine) or age (spirits), and some just repeat the name ('Añejo-class tequila.', 'Plata-style tequila.', 'Dry red.'). The gaps are flagged, not invented, but the menu reads as half-written. The layout makes it worse: 4 cocktails get a whole column with about 36 pt gaps and empty space, while 10 items are packed into the right column, so the drinks categories are not treated equally.
fixes: Get ABV, brewery and pour size for all beer and cider, wine region and producer, and tequila and cognac brand and age from the venue now (the needs_input items 1 and 4 have been open since round 5), then print them as 'Style · ABV · pour' and 'Grape · Region' lines, because criterion 8 cannot pass 70 while every non-cocktail line is a stub.

Until that data arrives, write the spirits lines in guest language instead of taxonomy wording that repeats the name ('Añejo-class tequila.', 'Plata-style tequila.', 'Grape brandy, VSOP grade.'), using only draft or row facts, e.g. keep the draft 'pour' wording ('Blanco tequila pour.') rather than inventing age or tasting notes.

Balance the space between categories: cut the 36 pt cocktail item gaps and the empty space under Margarita, Manhattan and Old Fashioned, and give the recovered space to the right-column cards so beer, wine and spirits lines can breathe and carry full descriptions.

Make the cocktail serve cues consistent: Manhattan and Daiquiri name a glass but Margarita and Brown Butter Old Fashioned do not, so either name the glass on all four from the recipe_versions glassware or name it on none; and print the dairy (brown butter) allergen note once the venue confirms it.
Label the Brut Rosé price as glass or bottle, and put pour sizes in the headers once supplied (for example 'By the Glass · 6 oz'), so every price has a unit and the price format reads as one system.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The flow puts the space in the wrong place. The cocktail card holds 4 items across half the page, with large dead gaps between Margarita, Manhattan and the House Originals. The 10 spirits, beer, cider and wine items are packed into small right-hand cards. House Originals (Brown Butter Old Fashioned, the signature and highest-priced cocktail) sit below the Classics, out of the prime spot. The agave card has two tequilas plus a Cognac, so 'La Botella' does not read as a Mexican cantina's spirit story. Checked round-9/doc.json against build/draft_doc.json: all 14 items and prices match exactly (none missing, extra or changed). Section order (Cocktails, Spirits, Beer/Cider, Wine) is a deliberate, documented change from the draft and works for an agave-led cantina. Non-cocktail descriptions are only the draft's words (for example 'Plata-style tequila.', 'Añejo-class tequila.', 'Dry red.', 'Dry white.'). They read as category labels, not guest language, and have no grape/region, style/ABV or age. They are flagged as missing, not invented, which is why criterion 8 is not an automatic fail. Brut Rosé's price has no glass or bottle label and beer/wine have no pour sizes (both flagged, still open), which holds criterion 3 down.
fixes: Put House Originals first on El Cantarito (Brown Butter Old Fashioned at the top-left prime spot, House Daiquiri next), then Classics, and close up the dead vertical gaps so the cocktail card's item spacing matches the other cards.

Rebalance the page: shrink the jug illustration on the featured card and give the recovered height to the right column so spirits, beer and wine get the same item and description spacing as the cocktails.

Get the missing facts from the venue through the Coordinator (tequila brands and ages, Cognac house, beer ABV and cider producer, wine grape/region for Brut Rosé and region for Malbec and Pinot Grigio). Then rewrite the category-label lines ('Plata-style tequila.', 'Añejo-class tequila.', 'Dry red.') as short guest-language descriptions built only from those facts.
Settle the Brut Rosé glass-or-bottle question and pour sizes with the venue, then print a label ('glass' / 'bottle' / oz) next to every wine and draft price so each price has a clear serve.

Move Cognac VSOP out of the agave story, or rename the card's framing so a brandy under 'La Botella' does not break the cantina narrative. Keep Spirits directly after Cocktails, since that order suits a Mexican bar.

top_problem: The menu speaks in two voices. The four cocktails get appetising guest copy with an italic serve cue, but the ten other items get catalogue labels ('Añejo-class tequila.', 'Grape brandy, VSOP grade.', 'Plata-style tequila.', 'Dry red.', 'Dry white.', 'Hop-forward, on draft.'). So spirits, beer and wine read like a different, unfinished menu and are not treated equally. The featured card also pads its four cocktails with 36 pt voids while the right cards pack items at 0 gap, so the text itself shows the imbalance.
fixes: Rewrite every non-cocktail line in the same guest voice as the cocktails, using only draft facts. Drop taxonomy words like 'class', 'grade' and 'style', and drop lines that repeat what the subheader already says ('on draft' under DRAFT). Where there are no facts yet (ABV, region, producer, brand, pour), show a visible placeholder such as 'ABV tbc' or 'region tbc' rather than a thin two-word line.
Give Brut Rosé a glass or bottle label (its price label is empty in the draft and flagged). Add a Glass label to the by-the-glass wines so every wine price says what it buys.

Either put Spirits after Wine to follow the scorecard flow (cocktails, beer, wine, spirits), or state in the cantor or cartouche copy why spirits lead as the agave story. Right now the change from the draft order is only explained in proposal.md, not on the menu.

Replace the verses that insult or joke about the guest ('La herramienta del borracho', 'que quedó como barril') and the off-topic 'enaguas' rhyme with lotería lines that invite rather than mock. Have the venue approve them, because they are the loudest copy on the page.
Put a dairy note on Brown Butter Old Fashioned (the allergen flag is unresolved). Replace the placeholder title 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' with the venue's real name, or flag it as needs_input.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged
top_problem: Missing data is flagged honestly in doc.json, but the printed menu hides the gaps with filler lines. 'Añejo-class tequila.', 'Plata-style tequila.', 'Dry red.', 'Dry white.' and 'Dry and sparkling.' (printed twice) mostly repeat the item name. So half the menu (spirits, beer, cider, wine) has no ABV, age, region or producer. The flags also mix real missing facts with admin questions, and the garnish and glass cues (lime wheel, orange peel, lime coin, coupe) cite 'recipe' with no row id. Those items are marked missing_ingredients: [] even though the cues are not traced to a source.
fixes: Give every printed garnish and glass cue (Margarita lime wheel, Old Fashioned orange peel, Daiquiri lime coin, Manhattan and Daiquiri coupe) its phg.recipe_versions row id in the source table, or drop the cue and add it to missing_ingredients. Right now Margarita and Daiquiri show missing_ingredients: [] while citing 'none'.

Keep missing_ingredients for missing guest-facing facts only (ABV, region, age, producer, pour size). Move 'venue to confirm the component-visibility flag', 'allergen confirmation' and 'guest line' into needs_input questions. Separately, hold 'aromatic bitters' on the Manhattan until the venue answers, because public_components aromatic-bitters = false and the draft line is not a sign-off.

Replace the name-echo spirit lines with a flagged placeholder state the Coordinator can see, such as a short 'awaiting brand and age' marker in doc.json and no filler text in print. 'Añejo-class tequila.' under 'Añejo Tequila' gives the guest nothing and hides the gap. Ask for the brand and age statement ahead of the pour sizes.

Brut Rosé has an empty price label but sits under 'Sparkling' with a bare 13, so print and phone both leave the guest guessing glass or bottle. Until the venue answers, print it with the same unit convention as By the Glass, or hold it out of print with the flag.

The Cocktails card has 36 pt gaps between items while every other card has 0 pt, which leaves large empty bands between cocktails. Yet same_item_gap_every_card reports True, so fix or explain that check. The item order also changed from the draft in two places (Spirits moved from 4th to 2nd, Margarita before Manhattan) and neither move is logged as a content change for the venue to approve.

lens: trace printed ingredients, garnishes, glass, serve and spirit lines to sources
top_problem: Every cocktail fact checks out. The three spirit lines are the weak point: 'Plata-style tequila.', 'Añejo-class tequila.' and 'Grape brandy, VSOP grade.' are wording lifted from the beverage_categories taxonomy (04d72e1f, 9f4dae69, a88f6e79/bec5063c), and 'Añejo-class tequila' only repeats the item name. That is an automatic-fail pattern for criterion 12. The lines are also inside a cantina's own agave story, so they drag down venue fit too.
verified: Margarita: rocks glass, lime wheel, method 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice' (recipe_versions via menu_items 14555870, gateway log 153). Components Fresh Lime Juice and Agave Syrup (prep) come from build/draft_doc.json. Printed 'Over fresh ice, lime wheel' is OK.

Manhattan: coupe and cocktail cherry (menu_items bf732e78, log 153) are OK. 'aromatic bitters' is in menu_description bf732e78, but draft_doc meta.public_components {'aromatic-bitters': false} hides it, so this is an open conflict and not verified for print.
Brown Butter Old Fashioned: orange peel, rocks, 'strain over a large cube' (menu_items 0cc4e912, log 153). Demerara Syrup and Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon are draft_doc preps. OK.
House Daiquiri: coupe, lime coin, fine strain (menu_items 44dcba6e, log 153). Draft_doc Demerara Syrup has the note 'House 1:1 demerara syrup'. OK.

Beer, cider and wine lines match the menu_items descriptions 90b0a7e3, 8fb136cd, 70657e1e, 65c39a14, f6f9d57e, 5ba7511f and 32a35bd3 with the name echo removed. Nothing invented. The Junmai Ginjo row 57617f46 is correctly left off.
Spanish accents in the verses and names are correct: cántaro, bebió, quedó, albañil, Añejo, Rosé.
problems: Criterion 12: the spirit lines use taxonomy wording ('-class', '-style', 'grade'). 'Añejo-class tequila' repeats the name. The draft's own guest wording ('Añejo tequila pour.', 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.', menu_items 124f8949, 19d79518, 75501d63) is no better. Real content (brand, age, pour size) is needed.

Criterion 12: 'Dry and sparkling.' is printed twice, for Dry Cider and Brut Rosé. 'Dry red.' and 'Dry white.' are two-word stubs next to cocktail copy of 12-18 words, so the menu reads in two different voices.

Criterion 14: the Cantarito card spreads four items with about 36 pt gaps and leaves large dead bands under Margarita and Manhattan. The right cards stack each description tight against the next item's name with a 0 pt gap. The same description system has two densities across the spread.
Criterion 14: Brut Rosé 13 has no glass or bottle label (the draft label is empty). Spirits and beer print no pour size, so the guest cannot tell what 12, 16 or 18 buys.
Criterion 11: the Manhattan 'aromatic bitters' contradicts the draft visibility flag public_components aromatic-bitters=false. It stays unverified until the venue decides.

That is a poor fit for a college-town bar that needs to reassure on responsible service. The cantina reads cocktail-bar-first, and the agave card gives two one-line tequila pours and no mezcal story.
fixes: Replace the three spirit lines with guest copy. If brand, age and pour size are still missing, print a neutral pour label (for example '1.5 oz pour', once the venue supplies it) or keep the item unfinished with a missing_ingredients flag. Do not print taxonomy classes.

Rebalance item spacing: put a consistent 6-9 pt gap after every description on all four cards and give the cocktail card's surplus depth to the face or the descriptions. Do not leave dead bands between items.

Give cider and rosé different lines, and bring the wine and beer lines up to the cocktail voice using only the draft words (for example 'Dry, sparkling rosé' in its Sparkling slot). If nothing more is sourced, flag them.
Resolve the Manhattan bitters conflict with the venue before printing. Until then, keep the current wording flagged in needs_input.
Add a glass or bottle label to Brut Rosé once confirmed, and swap the 'borracho' verse for a lotería card whose rhyme does not celebrate drunkenness (the venue may drop the verses).

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: There are two voices on one menu. The cocktails get guest copy, but the spirits card prints database class labels: 'Plata-style tequila.', 'Añejo-class tequila.' and 'Grape brandy, VSOP grade.' These are taxonomy wording, and 'Añejo-class tequila' only repeats the item name. That is an automatic criterion-12 fail under the scorecard. Beer, cider and wine are two-word stubs ('Dry red.', 'Dry white.'), and 'Dry and sparkling.' is printed twice, for Dry Cider and for Brut Rosé.
fixes: Replace the three spirits lines with guest language. The venue's own draft menu_description rows are 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.' and 'VSOP Cognac pour.' (phg.menu_items, gateway log_id 148). If those feel too thin, list them as missing_ingredients and ask for brand, age and tasting notes; do not dress up beverage_categories path names (04d72e1f, 9f4dae69, a88f6e79, bec5063c) as guest copy.

Give beer, cider and wine one sensory line each from the draft words, and stop printing the same words twice. Brut Rosé and Dry Cider both print 'Dry and sparkling.'; the draft rows are 'Dry sparkling rosé.' and 'Dry sparkling cider.' 'Hop-forward, on draft.' repeats the DRAFT subheader directly above it, so print 'Hop-forward.'

Resolve the Manhattan bitters conflict before print. The draft doc sets public_components {'aromatic-bitters': false}, and the printed line still shows 'aromatic bitters'. menu_items bf732e78 does say 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.', but the visibility flag is the venue's more specific instruction, so drop the bitters or get the venue to confirm.

Layout note for the designer (criterion 14): the featured cocktail card has large dead bands between items (roughly 36 pt plus leftover space after Margarita, Manhattan and the Old Fashioned). The right-hand cards have no gap at all, so the BRANDY, CIDER and SPARKLING subheaders sit tight under the line above. Brut Rosé's price has no glass/bottle label and no pour size is printed anywhere. The bold terracotta italic serve cue is the same colour as the prices and competes with them.

Venue fit (criterion 13): for a cantina, the cocktail card leads with Margarita but then goes Manhattan, Old Fashioned, Daiquiri with no agave follow-through. The spirits list is two tequilas and a cognac. Put agave first in the emphasis, and check with the venue about 'La herramienta del borracho' ('the drunkard's tool') as a headline verse over spirits in a college town (responsible-service tone).

lens: venue-type fit (Mexican cantina and cocktail bar, Spanish and lotería usage incl. verses, census ZIP 52240)
top_problem: The Spanish is right. All four cantor verses are the correct traditional lotería lines with correct accents (cántaro, enaguas, bebió, albañil, quedó), and Añejo and Rosé are spelled correctly. The problem is what those cards hold. EL CANTARITO is also the name of a well-known tequila-and-grapefruit drink served in a clay jar, but that drink is not on the menu, and the card holding it is 3/4 non-Mexican classics (Manhattan, Old Fashioned, Daiquiri). The deck also has no mezcal, no Mexican beer (the draft pours a Czech Pilsner) and 'Plata-style' / 'Añejo-class' / 'VSOP grade' taxonomy lines. So the lotería works as decoration, but the menu does not read as a cantina. For ZIP 52240, cocktails at $14-16 and pours at $12-18 sit at the top of the price range. The census row: median age 28.6, median household income $52,960, 29.9% aged 21-34, 11% Hispanic/Latino, 26.1% of households over $100k (phg_census_zcta 52240, ACS 2020-2024, gateway log_id 152).

verified.sources_ok: Every cocktail glass, garnish and serve traces to phg.recipe_versions. Margarita f06abb74: Rocks, 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice', Lime wheel. Manhattan 9fb77eaa: Coupe, Cocktail cherry. House Daiquiri 14d45e57: Coupe, Lime coin. Brown Butter Old Fashioned 7095fd3d: Rocks, 'strain over a large cube', Orange peel. Manhattan's 'aromatic bitters' matches its menu_description, 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.' Beer, cider and wine lines trace to the phg.menu_items menu_description text. All prices match phg.menu_items (gateway log_id 152).
verified.weak_sources: 'Plata-style tequila.' rests only on the beverage_categories name 'Blanco / plata' (04d72e1f). 'Añejo-class tequila.' repeats the item name, and the source row 9f4dae69 is itself noted as 'nothing printable'. 'Grape brandy, VSOP grade.' is a taxonomy path (a88f6e79, bec5063c), not guest language. Spirits and wine are missing brand, producer, region, vintage and pour size, and Brut Rosé has no glass/bottle label. These are correctly flagged in needs_input.

problems: Criterion 12: the spirits lines ('Plata-style tequila.', 'Añejo-class tequila.', 'Grape brandy, VSOP grade.') read as database classes, and the Añejo line echoes the item name. 'Dry red.' and 'Dry white.' are one-word stubs, in a different voice from the full cocktail sentences.

Criterion 13: EL CANTARITO names a well-known cocktail that is not on the menu. The cocktail card leads with Margarita, then non-Mexican classics. Agave is only 2 items, with no mezcal. The beer list has no Mexican-style lager. LA ROSA as the wine card is a loose fit. Prices sit at the high end for a student ZIP (median income $52,960).

Criterion 14: the two columns are unevenly spaced. The featured card has 36 pt voids between items (large blank areas under Margarita and Manhattan). The right cards run items with a 0 pt gap, and the BRANDY, CIDER and SPARKLING subheads sit tight against the description above them. Spirits and wine prices carry no pour label, and Brut Rosé's price has no glass/bottle label.

Criterion 10: the full-sentence cocktail copy with italic serve cues and the fragment copy on the other cards read like two different menus. The loose left column and cramped right column make the page feel uneven.
fixes: Replace the spirits taxonomy lines with guest-language lines built only from what the venue supplies (brand, age statement, pour), and keep them flagged until then. Never print 'class', 'grade' or '-style'.

Keep the cocktails under EL CANTARITO only if the venue confirms a Cantarito is served. Otherwise rename that card to a lotería card with no drink clash, or send the Coordinator a note asking whether a Cantarito should be added.
Designer: bring the 36 pt featured-card gaps and the 0 pt right-card gaps into one rhythm, and add 6-12 pt of space above every subhead on the right cards.
Once the venue answers, print pour and format labels (1.5 oz / 2 oz, glass or bottle for Brut Rosé) next to the prices.

Send the Coordinator a venue-fit note: a cantina in 52240 should show mezcal and a Mexican lager, and cocktail pricing should be checked against the student-heavy ZIP. The item list and prices are not the reviewer's to change.

lens: descriptions and prices laid out together in the print PNG (preview-letter.png), facts checked against phg.menu_items + phg.recipe_versions for project ddc4bb5b (gateway log_id 150)
top_problem: The two columns lay out descriptions in two different ways. On the left, El Cantarito has 36 pt item gaps that leave large empty holes under Margarita (about 60 pt) and Manhattan (about 100 pt), so its descriptions float away from the next item. On the right, the cards have 0 pt item gaps, so each one-line description runs straight into the next item name or subheader (Añejo desc into BRANDY, Amber Lager desc into CIDER, Pinot Grigio desc into SPARKLING). The right column's copy is also taxonomy. 'Plata-style tequila.' and 'Añejo-class tequila.' repeat the item name as a category label, and 'Dry red.' / 'Dry white.' are two-word stubs. That reads as a second, weaker voice next to the rich cocktail copy.

fixes: Criterion 14: set one item rhythm on every card. Take the cocktail card's gap down to 12-24 pt and move the space it frees to the right-hand cards, so every description has at least half a line of air before the next item or subheader. Send this to the designer as a layout note.

lens: descriptions and prices laid out together on the phone PNG (round-9 preview-phone.png)
top_problem: On the phone, Brut Rosé ($13) and every spirit, beer and wine price have no serve or pour label (glass/bottle, pour size, pint size). The Brut Rosé price is the clear case of an unlabelled glass/bottle price. The spirits lines are written in taxonomy wording ('Plata-style tequila.', 'Añejo-class tequila.', 'Grape brandy, VSOP grade.'), and the beer and wine lines are 1-3 words that repeat the item name ('Dry red.', 'Dry white.', 'Toasty amber lager.'). So only the four cocktails have a real description-plus-price unit; everything below them reads as a price list. Verified against phg.menu_items / phg.recipe_versions for project ddc4bb5b (gateway log_id 149). Glass and garnish all match: Margarita rocks / lime wheel / 'strain over fresh ice'; Manhattan coupe / cocktail cherry, printed description 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.'; Brown Butter Old Fashioned rocks / orange peel / 'over a large cube'; House Daiquiri coupe / lime coin. Every price matches (15, 15, 16, 14, 12, 16, 18, 7, 8, 7, 8, 12, 11, 13). The small additions are the word 'fresh' on the Daiquiri lime (draft says 'White rum, lime, and house demerara syrup.') and 'syrup' on the Old Fashioned demerara (draft says 'demerara, bitters.'). Treat these as mild embellishment unless the draft-doc components cited in proposal.md back them. I did not verify the three beverage_categories spirit lines with a query (limited to 2 calls); I scored them as sourced but as taxonomy wording. Junmai Ginjo ($12) is in phg.menu_items but correctly left off and flagged in proposal.md (question 6).
fixes: Give each price its serve: spirits '1.5 oz' (or 'pour'), beer the pint or glass size, wine the 'glass' size, and a 'glass' or 'btl' label on Brut Rosé once the venue answers question 2. Until then keep it flagged and do not publish it unlabelled.

Rewrite the spirits lines in guest voice from the draft plus the cited beverage_categories rows, e.g. 'Unaged blanco tequila, served neat.' instead of 'Plata-style tequila.'. Drop the '-style', '-class' and 'grade' wording.

Give the wines and beers one appetising line with a second fact from the draft or data (grape or region for wine, style or ABV for beer), or flag missing_ingredients. Do not print 1-3 words that repeat the name ('Malbec: Dry red.').

Layout note for the designer: on the 390 px phone, short names like Malbec, Czech Pilsner and Dry Cider sit at the far left and the price at the far right, joined only by a faint dotted hairline, so the price looks detached. Strengthen the leader contrast or move the price closer to the name on phone only.
Remove 'fresh' from the Daiquiri lime and 'syrup' from the Old Fashioned demerara unless a recipe_components or draft-doc row prints them, so every word traces to a row.
